Opened for the discovery reference 'Kiddushin 40b'. Opened SEFARIA:Kiddushin.40b: a person should see himself half liable, half meritorious; one mitzvah 'tips himself to the pan of merit' (לכף זכות). Shares ¶13's two pans with the self on the scale.

Opened for the discovery reference 'Mishnah Avot 1:14'. Opened SEFARIA:Pirkei_Avot.1.14 (Hillel, cf. 1:12): 'If I am not for myself, who is for me? If I am only for myself, what am I?' Shares ¶25's self as closest friend and exit only with others.
Opened for the discovery reference 'Mishnah Avot 1:6'. Opened: acquire a companion; judge everyone favourably. Companionship theme belongs to 103:3; Avot 1:14 carries ¶25's point precisely.

Opened for the discovery reference 'Mishnah Avot 2:1'. Opened: 'reckon the loss of a commandment against its reward and the gain of a transgression against its loss'; the merchant's comparison of ¶6 applied to deeds.

Opened for the discovery reference 'Mishnah Avot 2:15'. Opened: the day is short, the work much, the wage great. Time and work, but framed as labour and wage; ¶9's time-as-capital is carried by Ps 90:12 and Eph 5:16.
Opened for the discovery reference 'Mishnah Avot 2:16'. Opened: you need not finish the work; the employer pays. Wage theme, 103:3-adjacent; no page claim.
Opened for the discovery reference 'Mishnah Avot 2:4'. Opened: Hillel: do not separate from the community. Close to ¶25 but Avot 1:14 states the self/others structure more exactly; duplicate.
Opened for the discovery reference 'Mishnah Avot 3:1'. Opened: know before whom you will give account and reckoning (דין וחשבון). Generic reckoning formula; Avot 3:16's open ledger carries ¶7.
Opened for the discovery reference 'Mishnah Avot 3:15'. Opened: all is according to the majority of deeds. The majority principle is presented more concretely in Kiddushin 40b at ¶13.

Opened for the discovery reference 'Mishnah Avot 3:16'. Opened: the shop is open, the ledger open, the hand writes, collectors exact payment 'with or without his knowledge'. Shares ¶7's ledger read regardless of the person's awareness.

Opened for the discovery reference 'Mishnah Avot 4:1'. Opened: who is rich? he who rejoices in his lot. Defines wealth by contentment (a feeling), the opposite axis of ¶5-7's ledger; no paragraph turns on it.
Opened for the discovery reference 'Mishnah Avot 4:16'. Opened: this world a vestibule before the world to come. Generic eschatology.
Opened for the discovery reference 'Mishnah Avot 4:17'. Opened: one hour of repentance and good deeds in this world. Time and deeds (103:1/103:3), not 103:2.
Opened for the discovery reference 'Mishnah Avot 4:22'. Opened: all is according to the reckoning; you will give account. Generic; covered by Avot 3:16.

Opened for the discovery reference 'Rosh Hashanah 16b'. Opened in full: R. Yitzhak's sayings on judgment and R. Kruspedai's three books (wholly righteous, wholly wicked, intermediate). The scale-of-merit point at ¶13 is carried by Kiddushin 40b; the books add no 103:2-specific point.
Opened for the discovery reference 'Shabbat 153a'. Opened: R. Eliezer: repent one day before your death, i.e. every day. Time and repentance, not loss or scale.

Opened for the discovery reference 'Shabbat 31a'. Opened (later part): Rava: when a person is brought to judgment he is asked first 'Did you deal (buy and sell) in faith?' Shares ¶11's link of market honesty with the great day.

Opened for the discovery reference 'Ta'anit 23a'. Opened in full: Honi sleeps seventy years, is not recognised, prays for death; Rava: 'either companionship or death'. Close to ¶25, but Avot 1:14 and Eccl 4:8-10 already carry the point; omitted to keep one block per point.
